items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: Richard Berkey, he was Bobby Darin’s conductor

ctx.x: That’s right maybe we’ll cut that out. You must have gotten your reading together some if you’re going to do studio work.

Oh yeah. Believe me, I did get it together. There was an awful lot of studio work that came up, there was lots of shows that I worked at the Copa Cabana and places like that where people would come in and we just simply had to read. And then the studio work started because I did an album for this producer named Bob Thompson, and Richard Berkey, he was Bobby Darin’s conductor, and I sort of lured him to New York, and Richard Berkey wrote an album of stuff. And what happened was I played a solo on “I’ll Be Seeing…
You still have a copy I would assume.
